questions.question:

__
 
• **Sustain** means keeping** something alive for a long period** of time. 

 
 
• **Example**: *Ron **sustained** despite his peer pressure.*

• **Example:** *Luke **endured** his family's financial needs despite his meagre salary. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, support is the most appropriate synonym for sustain.

• **Example:** *The police **suspect** William's gang for the burglary. *

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The examinations / will be pushed back / so that candidates get additional time / for prepare.

options.text: so that candidates get additional time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**for prepare**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prepare** is a **verb**. In order to explain a verb, the preposition "**to**" is always used.

 
 
• **Example:** *Lucy needs some coriander leaves **to** **garnish** her dish.*
 
 
 
• The preposition "**for**" is used to explain a **noun**.
 
 
• **Example**: *English is a language used **for** **communication.** *
 
 
 
• Therefore, the appropriate sentence should have been "The examinations will be pushed back so that candidates get additional time to prepare".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **verb** "prepare" can also be changed as a **noun** to justify the proposition.
 
• The noun of prepare is **preparation**.
 
• Therefore, the sentence would change to "*The examinations will be pushed back so that candidates get additional time for preparation*".

Either Sumit or Amit will give __their__ assistance in unloading the goods from the truck.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**his**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The pronoun "**their**" is used to denote **pluralism**.

 
 
• **Example:** *Mr and Mrs Henry are getting **their** house painted. *
 
 
 
• The pronoun "**his**" is **singular**, used to denote **masculine** gender.
 
 
• **Example**:* Let me get **his** shirt ironed.* 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, only **one person** is giving his assistance, which means it is singular.
 
• Therefore, the appropriate option is "his".

• **Your** - **second person** pronoun which denotes the **person who is listening**.

 
 
• **Example:** *Give me **your **opinion on this proposal.* 
 
 
 
• **Its** - **third person** pronoun which denotes an **object**.
 
 
• **Example:** *The dog played with **its** toys. *

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Its matter of great concern / for the authorities that / despite all the efforts, / the number of patients is increasing.

options.text: the number of patients is increasing

questions.solution:
The answer is "**Its matter of great concern**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The phrase** "Its matter of great concern" does **not contain an article**. 
 
• As it discusses about only **one** matter, the article "**a**" is missing.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase would be "**Its a matter of great concern**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**A**", "**an**" and "**the**" are the **articles** used in English.
 
• "**A**" is used in front of **singular** words that does **not start with a vowel**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Please give me **a** slice of cake.*
 
 
 
• "**An**" is used in front of **singular** words **beginning with a vowel**. 
 
 
• **Example**: *Can I have **an** ice cream today?*
 
 
 
• "**The**" is used to denote a **particular object.**
 
 
• **Example:** *Give me **the** Oxford dictionary. *

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

__Despite play__ very well, we lost the match.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**despite playing**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Play**" is used in **simple present tense** if the noun in **plural**. The noun in the given sentence is **singular**. 
 
• "**Playing**" is in the **continuous tense** which shows an **on going action**.
 
• To justify the **subject verb concord **in the given sentence, **continuous tense** must be used because during the match, playing was going on, that is, it was continuous. .
 
• Therefore, the option "despite playing" is appropriate. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The three basic types of tenses are **present, past and future.**
 
• **Present tense** - denotes the action happening **now**.
 
 
• **Example**: *Nancy **eats** a sandwich. *
 
 
 
• **Past tense** - denotes an action already **happened**. 
 
 
• **Example**: *Nancy **ate** a sandwich yesterday. *
 
 
 
• **Future tense** - denotes an action that is **yet to happen**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Nancy **will eat** her sandwich after an hour.*
 
 
 
• All these tenses are further divided as **simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.**

**The correct sentence is:** *This is the garage **where** I get my car repaired.*
